page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs. The memory configuration is a key highlight, offering 64.0 GB of RAM, which equates to a high resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate to weak processing profile. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, though small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic and compression tasks show lower-tier performance, with single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression falling in the bottom 10%. However, the server maintains average performance for Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high-frequency CPU performance. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs positions it as a specialized option for memory-bound applications. Recommended workloads include caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis, and lightweight data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, this instance provides 8.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Network performance is anchored by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark data reveals a modest performance profile, with CPU and memory bandwidth tests generally scoring in the lower-to-average tiers. While single-core compute and compression speeds are weak, the instance achieves average throughput in Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and moderate compute capabilities, the ecs.se1.2xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and general-purpose memory-bound applications.
